statements.text: FDA recognizes that the increased use of AI, including ML, across all our regulated industries presents new and unique opportunities and challenges.
statements.context: FDA officials testify before the House Energy and Commerce Health Subcommittee on the Agency's regulation of drugs, biologics, and devices, including its approach to AI/ML.

statements.text: we have to be more productive and continue to be more productive, and AI gives us the opportunity to be more productive. We have to outpace our competitors, and particularly in Asia and China, and AI gives us a great opportunity to do so.
statements.context: Opening remarks at a House subcommittee hearing on AI in manufacturing and U.S. competitiveness.

statements.text: And in his book ``Genesis'' he wrote with—the last book written by Henry Kissinger—just really lays out the need to win the battle of AI against China.
statements.context: Speaking at a hearing on electricity demand, the lawmaker argues that AI competition with China requires abundant U.S. power generation.

statements.text: we built a program that we want to get good, structured data into our system that helps us get good, structured data and it allows us to utilize large language modeling machine learning and, to a certain point, some generative AI to predict when we may have a duplicate payment or the payment doesn't actually check the box for the contract. [...] And we are detecting, just in the recent months, we had three situations for about $600,000 that we flagged for potential fraud, waste, or abuse.
statements.context: Verbatim congressional hearing testimony on FEMA reform, discussing use of AI for fraud detection in emergency-management payments.

statements.text: if the world's existential threat is climate change, or if you believe it—I am simplifying this to two. [...] dominating AI over—being the world platform for AI.
statements.context: Closing remarks by Rep. Guthrie during a House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on regional grid reliability, pivoting to the strategic stakes of AI competition with China.

statements.text: And the complicated question of how to deliver that power effectively is compounded by the tremendous increase in demand projected over coming years for specific purposes like AI, and broader increases in consumer demand. [...] So here in Congress we must identify and understand the forces impacting the ability of engineers to plan and operate this system for better or for worse. And we must address the commonsense policy reforms that will allow utilities and operators to do their work cost-effectively.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Brett Guthrie at a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on regional grid reliability.

statements.text: And I had an opportunity that—we are actually going to have a great opportunity in a couple of weeks to have a hearing with Eric Schmidt [...] wrote a book with Henry Kissinger called ``Genesis,'' presented it at the Library of Congress, and I walked away with my mouth open, my heart beating, going, ``Wow, this is the fight of our lives. Are we going to win the AI battle with China?''
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on regional grid reliability, where the member pivots from energy policy to AI competition with China.

statements.text: I’m particularly concerned about one of these harms: the use of AI and other digital technologies to maliciously target women and children through exploiting deepfake, non-consensual intimate images. [...] The TAKE IT DOWN Act adopts a common-sense approach to stop the spread of malicious deepfake pornography and grants survivors’ new rights to request that non-consensual images of themselves be removed from the internet.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Chairman Guthrie at a House Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee hearing on online harms.

statements.text: And to sum up what you said, it is the U.S. versus China, and who will win the war for AI. [...] we have to have broad consensus on how we work together, it has to be Democrat and Republican.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Guthrie at a full Energy and Commerce Committee hearing on AI technology and American competitiveness.

statements.text: What I would like to do in this committee is come up with a regulatory framework and an energy policy that most of us can agree on and build a broad consensus on how we develop massive amounts of energy while protecting our environment.
statements.context: Opening statement by House Energy and Commerce Chairman Brett Guthrie at a full-committee hearing on AI, energy, and U.S. competitiveness.

statements.text: If we don't meet the energy demand, we are not going to win the battle for AI, and that is catastrophic, I think, for our country.
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on energy infrastructure needs for AI and innovation, chaired by Rep. Guthrie.

statements.text: When we talk about the demand for energy because of AI technologies that are coming and—I mean, one answer is they don't come, but if we don't come, they are going to go somewhere, and they are going to go to China. So that is not an option. But, if they come on and demand energy, it competes with energy that is available for the people in their homes and seniors in their homes and things. So we have to expand our energy resources.
statements.context: House hearing on assuring abundant American energy to power innovation, where Guthrie questions a DOE official about grid expansion needs.

statements.text: We are at a crossroads. The decisions we make on AI regulation are critical and will determine whether we allow innovation to flourish or risk falling behind on the global stage.
statements.context: Chairman Guthrie delivers opening remarks at a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology hearing on AI regulation and US leadership.

statements.text: The big fear that we can't do, I don't think, is that there is this idea that you could take the AI, the algorithm, and send it off to an FDA-style entity and get them to approve it and send it back and say, ``Yeah, you can do it,'' while China is just turning them out. And we saw what happened with DeepSeek. Their chips are not as good as ours, but it should wake us all up.
statements.context: Congressman Brett Guthrie questions a witness at a hearing titled 'AI Regulation and the Future of U.S. Leadership.'

statements.text: And through major investments to modernize the Department of Commerce, we will integrate AI systems and upgrade IT systems to make the Department more secure and effective. To protect the integrity of this project, we are implementing guardrails that protect against State-level AI laws that could jeopardize our technological leadership.
statements.context: Floor statement by Representative Guthrie during debate on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, summarizing Energy and Commerce Committee reconciliation provisions.

statements.text: So to beat China we have to win the AI battle, and that is energy and making sure we have the right regulatory structure.
statements.context: House hearing on AI regulation and U.S. leadership where a member questions witnesses about the impact of EU-style regulation on startups.

statements.text: So, Mr. Vasishta, we have been focused on—almost every hearing that we have had has been focused on how do we beat China to AI.
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology, questioning an NVIDIA executive about data center energy efficiency.

statements.text: As such, it is important that we take a measured approach and strike the right balance between facilitating innovation and providing principled guardrails where needed to address gaps in current law.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Brett Guthrie at a House Energy and Commerce subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology.

statements.text: Right now, we are fighting to achieve AI dominance. It is a technological race that we cannot afford to lose to China.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Brett Guthrie at a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on the FY 2026 DOE budget, addressed to Energy Secretary Chris Wright.

statements.text: These overly restrictive air regulations oppress domestic investments in semiconductor plants and data centers, jeopardizing America’s ability to compete in the global AI race.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Energy and Commerce Environment Subcommittee hearing on Clean Air Act modernization and infrastructure permitting.

statements.text: autonomous vehicles account and utilize AI for sensing classification, prediction, decision making. In many ways AVs present a real-world application of AI with transformative potential. One of the themes that we have had— or the theme, I guess you want to say, defining theme of this first 6 months of most of the committee has been American global leadership in AI. Our values or China's values in AI. Could you talk about how continued advancement in deployment of AVs can help America's global leadership in AI?
statements.context: House Energy and Commerce Committee hearing on NHTSA and motor vehicle safety, where a member questions a witness about AVs and AI competitiveness.

statements.text: As chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, one of my top priorities is ensuring that America has the energy needed to win the race for AI against China and power our future.
statements.context: House floor speech by the chairman of the Energy and Commerce Committee advocating for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's energy, spectrum, and healthcare provisions.

statements.text: I want to emphasize that AI is in no way intended to overtake the jobs of hard-working Americans.
statements.context: Opening statement by the Chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health at a hearing on AI in American health care.

statements.text: But in recent months, we have seen deeply troubling headlines about children and adults alike suffering harms as a result of AI chatbot interactions.
statements.context: Opening statement by the chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations at a hearing on AI chatbot risks and benefits.

statements.text: Ten years after Russia conducted the world’s first largescale cyberattack in Ukraine that shut down the grid for 200,000 residents, we witnessed the first documented largescale AI-driven cyberattack against governments, financial institutions, and businesses around the globe last month.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Brett Guthrie at a House Energy Subcommittee hearing on securing America's energy infrastructure against cyber and physical threats to the grid.

statements.text: Scientists, AI company executives, and national security experts are expressing concerns about the increasing risks of misusing AI to develop dangerous biological weapons or novel pathogens.
statements.context: Opening statement by the chairman of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations at a hearing on AI and biosecurity.

statements.text: TITLE IV—ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CHATBOTS [...] A chatbot provider may not provide to a covered user a chatbot that states to the covered user that the chatbot is a licensed professional (unless such statement is true). [...] A chatbot provider shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to each covered user of a chatbot [...] (1) The chatbot is an artificial intelligence system and not a natural person. (2) Resources for contacting a suicide and crisis intervention hotline.
statements.context: Floor introduction of H.R. 7757, the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act, in the U.S. House of Representatives.
